title: The small pro-etale topos has enough points
statement: Let $X$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], and take its small pro-etale site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with the compatible universes and small-skeleton convention of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. There exists a set-indexed family of points $p_i:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{proet}})$, where point means a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism], whose inverse-image functors jointly reflect isomorphisms: a morphism $a:F\to G$ of sheaves of sets is an isomorphism if all $p_i^{-1}a$ are bijections. These are arbitrary points of the topos; they are not asserted to be the ordinary geometric points of the scheme.

source.place: Tag 0992, label lemma-points-proetale, assertion for the small site S_proetale

proof.text: Let $\mathcal A=X_{\mathrm{aff,proet}}$ be the full subsite of affine weakly etale objects with standard finite affine coverings. By [lem-sfb-proetale-affine-subsite-equivalence], restriction gives an equivalence $E:\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{proet}})\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal A)$. We will verify the finitary-slice criterion on $\mathcal A$.

source.place: Tag 098W, lemma-alternative; small-site part of the proof of Tag 0992, lemma-points-proetale

proof.text: Index by every object $U$ of the chosen small skeleton of $\mathcal A$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $h_U=(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(-,U))^\#$ using [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The canonical map $e:\coprod_U h_U\to1$ is epic: if $a,b:1\to F$ agree after $e$, they agree after every $h_U\to1$ and hence after the unit $\operatorname{Hom}(-,U)\to h_U$. Evaluating those equal composites at $\operatorname{id}_U$ gives $a_U(*)=b_U(*)$. This holds for every $U$, so $a=b$ as natural transformations [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. This proves the required representable-cover assertion directly, without subcanonicity or a cover of a non-affine terminal scheme.

source.place: Tag 00YN, lemma-criterion-points, hypothesis (1): elementary verification using all objects and the sheafification unit

proof.text: Fix $U\in\mathcal A$. For a cospan $V\to T\leftarrow W$ in $\mathcal A/U$, form $P=V\times_TW$ as a scheme [def-pc-fibre-product]. Since $V,T,W$ are affine [def-pc-scheme], choose spectrum presentations; their arrows correspond to ring homomorphisms by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The formula in [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $P$ with the spectrum of the corresponding tensor product, so $P$ is affine. The $X$-morphism $V\to T$ is weakly etale by [lem-trf-weakly-etale-between-objects], since $V\to X$ and $T\to X$ are weakly etale. Its base change $P\to W$ and then its composite $P\to X$ are weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. Thus $P\to X$ belongs to $\mathcal A$; its map to $U$ makes it an object of $\mathcal A/U$. The scheme universal property gives a unique map from every cone in this full slice category, so it is its pullback. This verifies affine-slice closure itself; no identification with a qcqs slice is used.

source.place: Tag 098M, lemma-fibre-products-proetale, affine fibre-product argument, expanded through the existing affine-spectrum and weakly-etale nodes

proof.text: The identity $U\to U$ is terminal in $\mathcal A/U$. Step 3 supplies all pullbacks there. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-limits-from-terminal-pullbacks](1) to obtain finite limits. By [lem-sfb-proetale-affine-subsite-equivalence], the chosen coverings of $\mathcal A$ are standard finite affine coverings; a covering in the slice has the same underlying family and is therefore finite itself. Taking this family as its own refinement verifies the finite-cover-refinement hypothesis, including the empty covering of the empty scheme. This argument requires only that the objects of $\mathcal A$ be affine, with no quasi-compactness or separatedness assumption on $X$.

source.place: Tags 098W and 0992: standard finite coverings on the affine subsite; slice finite limits from terminal objects and the affine pullbacks of Tag 098M

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-site-finitary-slice-enough-points] to $\mathcal A$, with all its objects as the set-indexed family: step 2 proves the epimorphism hypothesis and steps 3-4 prove both slice hypotheses. We get a conservative set of points $p_j:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal A)$. Compose these with the inverse of the equivalence $E$ of [lem-sfb-proetale-affine-subsite-equivalence]. An equivalence has an inverse adjunction and preserves all limits, by applying its inverse to the limit universal property, so this is a geometric morphism. By [def-trf-geometric-morphism], its inverse image is $p_j^{-1}E$. If all these functors send a morphism $a$ to bijections, conservativity makes $E(a)$ an isomorphism, and the inverse equivalence makes $a$ an isomorphism. The family remains set-indexed; its members are arbitrary topos points as asserted.
